summary: Regression testing after adding spring.jackson.property-naming-strategy=SNAKE_CASE to Spring Boot deliverable. Static check on application.properties confirmed. FastAPI preview regression: all 20 pytest tests pass; ROI API returns snake_case keys with expected values (35/55/35, 4.5, 260.0); insights returns 6+ posts with snake_case (image_url, read_minutes, published_at); contact CRUD works. Frontend ROI calculator submits successfully and renders '35%/55%/35%', 'Projected impact for Acme Corp', baseline '10 people · 400 hrs / week · Excel, SAP' — no 'undefined' anywhere.
critical_code_review_comments: Spring Boot fix is a single-line, low-risk config change — cannot be executed in this sandbox (no Maven/JDK runtime here), but the file was verified statically and the equivalent contract on FastAPI is confirmed correct end-to-end.
Recommendation for main agent: also add a compile-time DTO test in the Spring Boot project (e.g. using MockMvc + jsonPath('$.money_savings_pct')) so this regression is caught automatically in CI.
seed_data_creation: None new; insights seed remains from prior iterations
context_for_next_testing_agent: Spring Boot deliverable cannot be built/run in this sandbox — only static verification of application.properties is possible. FastAPI preview at REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL is the running contract and matches the frontend snake_case expectations. ROI endpoint requires body fields current_manpower, current_hours_per_week, current_tools (not manpower/hours_per_week/tools).
rca of the issue: Spring Boot's default Jackson property-naming strategy is LOWER_CAMEL_CASE, producing keys like moneySavingsPct while the React client (RoiCalculator.jsx) and the FastAPI preview both use snake_case (money_savings_pct). Setting spring.jackson.property-naming-strategy=SNAKE_CASE in application.properties makes Jackson serialize ALL controller responses in snake_case globally, aligning the Spring Boot deliverable with the frontend contract. Verified on FastAPI: response contains money_savings_pct=35, manpower_reduction_pct=55, time_reduction_pct=35, projected_manpower=4.5, projected_hours_per_week=260.0.
